tagline.text: An island of coral cliffs where sea turtles and jackfish circle

children.text: A small coral island about
2km

around, floating in the sea southwest of Panglao Island, where a sheer coral wall rings the island as a designated marine protected area. Sea turtle sightings are nearly guaranteed, making it a key destination for Bohol hopping tours and diving.
Balicasag Island is a small, flat coral island about
6–7km
southwest of Alona Beach on Panglao Island. At about
2km
around — small enough to circle on foot in
30 minutes
— it consists of little more than a fishing village, a lighthouse, and a dive resort run by a government tourism agency, all administratively part of the Panglao municipality.

The island's real appeal lies underwater. The shallow coral flat at the island's edge drops away after just a few steps into a sheer coral wall plunging tens of meters deep, where fan corals and soft corals grow thick and every kind of reef fish gathers. Since the mid-

, part of the waters around the island has been managed as a no-fishing marine protected area, and thanks to that protection, sea turtles and huge schools of jackfish (trevally) linger without much fear of people.

Balicasag is ranked among Filipino divers as "Bohol's best wall diving," with well-known sites such as Black Forest, Divers Heaven, and Cathedral encircling the island. Even non-divers can join a guided snorkel to drift over the shallow coral and watch sea turtles come up for air.

Most travelers stop at Balicasag as one leg of a hopping tour departing Alona Beach at dawn. The most common route combines dolphin-watching, snorkeling at Balicasag, and the Virgin Island sandbar into a half-day trip, while divers typically do two to three dives around Balicasag in a day.
In the protected waters off the island, you tour the coral with a local guide, either by small boat or swimming. Sea turtles pass close by over the shallow coral at
depth.
A sloping site on the island's west side, named for the black whip corals growing like a forest. When there's current, chances are good of encountering turtles, jackfish, and barracuda.
A sheer coral wall on the island's south side, where you drift slowly along, taking in fan corals, sponges, lionfish, and turtles. On clear days, visibility can exceed
A whirling mass of hundreds of jackfish spinning like a tornado is one of Balicasag's signature sights. The odds are best while diving, but with luck it can also be seen snorkeling.
Hopping tours departing Alona Beach at
look for spinner dolphins on the way to Balicasag. After the dolphins, you head straight to Balicasag to snorkel in the clear early-morning water.

blocks.title: Beach walk and the island lighthouse

children.text: After snorkeling, landing on the island lets you explore the white sand beach, the small village, and the lighthouse. Beach stalls selling shell necklaces and fresh coconut juice are a good place to rest.

blocks.title: Stopping at the Virgin Island sandbar

children.text: On the way back from Balicasag, stopping at the sandbar that emerges at low tide for photos and a taste of sea-urchin dishes rounds off the hopping tour.

1 hour 20 minutes
from Manila to Bohol–Panglao International Airport (TAG). From the airport to Alona Beach is about
15–20 minutes
by car.
A fast craft such as OceanJet from Cebu takes about
2 hours
to Tagbilaran Port (about
); from Tagbilaran to Alona Beach is about

Balicasag has no scheduled ferry, so you go by bangka from a Panglao beach such as Alona. It takes about
30–40 minutes
from Alona; chartering the whole boat for the dolphin–Balicasag–Virgin Island route costs about
, while joining a shared tour with other travelers costs about
per person. Book through a tour booth, your accommodation, or a dive shop on Alona Beach.
Diving trips travel by the Alona Beach dive shop's boat, with the boat transfer included in the diving fee. The marine park entrance fee is often charged separately.
The waters around Balicasag are calmest and clearest from
March to June
, ideal for both snorkeling and diving. Water temperature stays warm year-round at 26–30°C, but from
December to February
the northeast monsoon raises waves and lowers the temperature slightly, so a 3mm-or-thicker wetsuit is more comfortable.
During the rainy season,
June–November

, showers are frequent and the sea can turn rough in the afternoon due to the southwest monsoon. When a typhoon or tropical depression passes, the coast guard bans small-boat departures, which can lead to tour cancellations.
Early morning is best. The sea is calm, the low sun brightens the water, and you'll wait less to snorkel before the group tour boats arrive. During peak season,
March–May
, and holidays, the protected area gets very crowded after

A government tourism-agency dive resort on Balicasag Island itself does allow an overnight stay, but with few rooms and limited amenities, most people base themselves on Alona Beach, Panglao Island, and visit for the day. Alona Beach offers a wide range from
guesthouses to
-or-more beach resorts.

The island itself has almost no proper restaurants — just beach stalls selling coconut juice, instant noodles, and simple snacks. If your tour boat doesn't include lunch, bring water and snacks. On the way back at Virgin Island, local vendors crack open sea urchins on the spot or sell mango and buko juice. For a proper meal, it's best to head back to Alona Beach for a seafood barbecue or Filipino home-style food.
The environmental fee and snorkeling fee are collected on site in cash. Confirm when booking whether they're included in the tour price.
Protected-area snorkeling requires a guide and you can't drift on your own. If you're not confident swimming, wear a life jacket and hold on to the tube the guide pulls.
Early morning gives the best odds of seeing sea turtles. Set your departure time so you arrive at the island around
7 AM
Bringing a waterproof camera or case lets you capture turtles and coral. Underwater, wrap the strap around your wrist to avoid losing it.
If you're prone to seasickness, take medication
30 minutes
before departure. The sea around Balicasag has more swell than it looks.
Smart and Globe signal is weak on the island. Agree on a meeting place and time with your group before you depart.
Divers should use a dive computer even with an Open Water certification, given how carefully depth must be managed on the wall.
Touching or riding sea turtles and coral is strictly prohibited and subject to a fine if caught. Keep at least
away from turtles.
Control your buoyancy so you don't stand on coral or kick it with your fins, and kick gently near the surface.
Some ingredients in ordinary sunscreen harm coral. Use a reef-safe product or a rash guard instead.
Currents can suddenly strengthen at wall diving sites. Stay close to your guide and keep to the planned depth.
The coast guard can ban departures in bad weather. Check the refund policy in advance in case your tour is cancelled.
Accelerating a hopping boat to chase dolphins, or crowding them with multiple boats, causes the animals great stress. Ask your boat driver to keep a distance.
